svg.title: What Dapr and a service mesh each do, and what they share
svg.desc: Two overlapping bands. The upper, wider band is Dapr and holds six building block APIs: service invocation, state management, publish and subscribe, bindings, secrets and actors. The lower band is the service mesh and holds traffic routing and traffic splitting, which Dapr does not provide. Where the two bands overlap sit the four capabilities both offer: mTLS, metrics, resiliency and distributed tracing. A strip above the bands holds the application code, in Go, Node.js, Python, Java, .NET, C++ or any other code or framework; a strip below holds the hosting infrastructure, on Azure, AWS, Google Cloud or Kubernetes. An axis down the right side runs from Developer at the top to Operator at the bottom: Dapr is developer-centric and a service mesh is infrastructure-centric.

g.text: Application code, in any language or framework
